articles.title: The EV Bust Creating a New Battery Boom
articles.description: Factories built to supply America’s electric-vehicle boom are getting a second life making batteries for the power grid. As EV demand weakens and electricity demand from data centers and new factories strengthens, battery makers are shifting toward stationary storage, but the new market still relies on federal incentives and a supply chain that remains partly dependent on China. The shift is visible at TransGrid’s Atlas projects in Arizona, where the contractor Qcells is using LG Energy Solution’s US-made battery cells. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Should You Buy Qualcomm Stock For Its Cash?
articles.description: Over the last twelve months, Qualcomm (QCOM) generated free cash flow equal to 5.5% of its market value. That outpaces the 4.4% yield for the median S&P 500 company. A yield above the median can mean a business that is either on sale or expected to shrink. Qualcomm's revenue fell in each of its last two quarters. So is that cash the sign of a business on sale, or of one that is shrinking.

articles.title: Federal Circuit Upholds PTAB Unpatentability Ruling Against Fungicide Combination Patent
articles.description: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (CAFC) issued a decision today in Syngenta Crop Protection AG v. UPL Ltd., affirming a Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) final written decision that held all challenged claims of a fungicide combination patent unpatentable. The CAFC rejected arguments from UPL Ltd. and affirmed the PTAB’s denial of leave for Syngenta Crop Protection AG to seek sanctions.
